vulnerabilities.description: Missing validation on memory file path - could theoretically allow writing to unintended locations if filesystem permissions are misconfigured. Currently mitigated by hardcoded directory.
Using spawnSync to execute git commands without shell escaping - safe implementation, but could be made more explicit about security measures.
SWC minification enabled - while beneficial for performance, limits source map availability for debugging. Not a security vulnerability but worth noting.
No package-lock.json pinning visible in git status - dependency versions should be locked to prevent supply chain attacks.
No explicit Content Security Policy (CSP) headers configured - would help prevent XSS and other injection attacks. Should add CSP headers in next.config.js.

recommendations: Add Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to next.config.mjs to mitigate XSS attacks
Ensure package-lock.json is committed and versions are pinned to prevent supply chain vulnerabilities
Regularly run 'npm audit' to check for vulnerable dependencies - current dependencies are relatively recent and well-maintained
Add HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security) headers when deploying to production
Implement rate limiting on any future API endpoints to prevent brute force attacks
Review localStorage usage to ensure no sensitive user data is persisted unencrypted
Verify that temporary files created in system tmpdir are being cleaned up properly (already implemented correctly)
Consider adding X-Frame-Options header to prevent clickjacking
Run security scan with 'npm audit' regularly
For production deployment, ensure all traffic is over HTTPS with security headers configured
positiveFindings: No hardcoded API keys, passwords, or secrets found in codebase
React application properly escapes user input to prevent XSS by default
Safe use of spawnSync() instead of shell execution - prevents command injection
Input validation on dynamic routes (categoria and calculadora parameters) with whitelist checking
No usage of dangerous functions like eval() or innerHTML with user input
Static Site Generation (SSG) architecture reduces attack surface - no server-side processing
Theme script properly isolated and only reads from secure localStorage
Form inputs use proper validation patterns (numeric, alphanumeric only)
Calculator functions use safe mathematical evaluation without eval()
Environment variables properly separated - only public vars (NEXT_PUBLIC_*) are exposed
Temporary files created with cryptographically secure randomBytes (8-byte hex)
Cleanup of temporary files implemented in finally block
rationale: The application demonstrates good security practices for a static calculator website. No critical vulnerabilities found. The main risks are around deployment configuration (CSP headers, HTTPS) rather than code-level issues. The architecture as a static site generation significantly reduces attack surface.

dependencyAudit.note: Dependencies are recent versions of well-maintained libraries. No known vulnerabilities at time of analysis.

testingRecommendations: Run: npm audit to check for vulnerable dependencies
Run: npm test to validate calculator logic
Add OWASP Top 10 security tests (SAST/DAST) to CI/CD pipeline
Implement regular security scanning in GitHub Actions
Test with Content Security Policy enabled
Verify no sensitive data in localStorage across all browsers
summary: This is a well-built static calculator website with minimal security risks. The main improvement would be adding HTTP security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options) during deployment. No critical code-level vulnerabilities were identified.
